data.claim: A mature participation platform produces mature democracy
data.interpretation: Describe platform capabilities separately from process quality, institutional response and outcomes.
data.uncertainty: Software maturity, feature breadth and deployment count do not establish inclusion, legitimacy, decision authority or implementation.

data.title: A merge audit trail improves trust and correction
data.claim: A merge audit trail improves trust and correction
data.interpretation: A reproducible import and merge ledger can make consolidation decisions reviewable and correctable.
data.uncertainty: Auditability can support accountability, but only if records are understandable, maintained, and open to challenge.

data.title: A method described in Participedia is suitable for reuse
data.claim: A method described in Participedia is suitable for reuse
data.interpretation: Use method records as option inputs; conduct local design, accessibility, power, safety, and legitimacy review before adoption.
data.uncertainty: Method pages describe purposes and features but cannot establish fit for a new community, legal context, conflict level, or power structure.

data.title: A movement-developed system is automatically community-controlled
data.claim: A movement-developed system is automatically community-controlled
data.interpretation: State the named organizational stewards and mark community decision rights as unresolved until documented.
data.uncertainty: Named movement involvement does not show how farmers, educators, contributors or territorial communities participate in consequential decisions.

data.title: A movement-led AI tool is automatically sovereign, safe or community-controlled
data.claim: A movement-led AI tool is automatically sovereign, safe or community-controlled
data.interpretation: Review governance, corpus, infrastructure dependencies, correction rights, affected users and evaluation before making sovereignty claims.
data.uncertainty: Movement sponsorship does not by itself resolve model dependence, data governance, access, bias, security or accountability.

data.title: A movement-owned school is automatically governed democratically
data.claim: A movement-owned school is automatically governed democratically
data.interpretation: Describe the movement relationship and separately review governance rules-in-use and participant authority.
data.uncertainty: Movement embedding and community identity do not reveal decision rules, accountability, resource control or internal inequalities.

data.title: A network of alternatives represents or validates all member practices
data.claim: A network of alternatives represents or validates all member practices
data.interpretation: Record the exact relationship and preserve the primary movement or community source.
data.uncertainty: Weavers and endorsers retain their own authority; network participation does not establish uniform agreement, effectiveness or legitimacy.

data.title: A neutral ontology can represent the field without exercising power
data.claim: A neutral ontology can represent the field without exercising power
data.interpretation: Treat ontology choices as governed and revisable decisions; record alternatives, disputes, and context.
data.uncertainty: Categories determine visibility, comparability, inclusion, and what appears normal or legitimate.

data.title: A Participation Playbook design is context-ready
data.claim: A Participation Playbook design is context-ready
data.interpretation: Use the Playbook as structured preparation alongside local expertise, affected-party design, and iterative review.
data.uncertainty: A guided tool cannot fully capture local politics, legal constraints, language, culture, conflict, safety, or institutional capacity.

data.title: A Participedia entry is a verified or peer-reviewed account
data.claim: A Participedia entry is a verified or peer-reviewed account
data.interpretation: Treat entries as structured, source-linked case syntheses with visible contribution history; verify consequential claims through primary and independent sources.
data.uncertainty: Entries may be crowdsourced, adapted from other sources, machine translated, or improved by staff editors, but this does not make them independently verified research.

data.title: A project appearing across several platforms is independently validated
data.claim: A project appearing across several platforms is independently validated
data.interpretation: Treat cross-platform presence as a relationship signal. Trace original sources and identify genuinely independent evidence.
data.uncertainty: Repeated visibility across directories, grants, analytics, registries or media can look like corroboration even when sources reuse the same self-reported information.

data.title: A prominent thinker represents the movement or community they write about
data.claim: A prominent thinker represents the movement or community they write about
data.interpretation: Use thinkers as situated lenses; retain movement, territorial and collective sources as primary where appropriate.
data.uncertainty: Visibility, publication and institutional position do not establish representative authority.

data.title: A proposal status proves implementation or impact
data.claim: A proposal status proves implementation or impact
data.interpretation: Display exact status, responsible body, date and evidence gaps.
data.uncertainty: Accepted, rejected or evaluating states are administrative records whose meaning depends on updating and evidence.

data.title: A public beta demonstrates adoption or usefulness
data.claim: A public beta demonstrates adoption or usefulness
data.interpretation: Record beta launch, intended users and available evidence; keep adoption and outcome claims unresolved until evaluated.
data.uncertainty: Launch and public demonstrations do not establish sustained use, access, accuracy, farmer trust, maintenance or outcomes.

data.title: A public mutual-aid directory verifies listed groups
data.claim: A public mutual-aid directory verifies listed groups
data.interpretation: Date records, avoid sensitive aggregation and confirm active status before referral.
data.uncertainty: Networks can change rapidly and public listings may be stale, incomplete or unsafe.

data.title: A public web interface demonstrates meaningful farmer access
data.claim: A public web interface demonstrates meaningful farmer access
data.interpretation: Describe the tool as publicly reachable; evaluate meaningful access through field and assisted-use testing.
data.uncertainty: Connectivity, device cost, literacy, language, disability access, trust, training and support affect real use.

data.title: A published methodology is universally valid
data.claim: A published methodology is universally valid
data.interpretation: A published Regen Registry protocol has completed a defined registry process; applicability and integrity must still be assessed for each context and project.
data.uncertainty: A published protocol is bounded to its scope, version, assumptions, review process, data requirements, and eligible contexts.

data.title: A research archive should make all underlying materials public
data.claim: A research archive should make all underlying materials public
data.interpretation: Use differentiated access, consent, redaction, retention, and community or ethics review rather than open-by-default release.
data.uncertainty: Protocols, transcripts, network files and datasets may contain personal, confidential, community-sensitive or reidentifiable information.

data.title: A seed submitted through the site is a reviewed commons contribution
data.claim: A seed submitted through the site is a reviewed commons contribution
data.interpretation: Treat submissions as raw participatory signals until routed, reviewed, and connected to stewardship.
data.uncertainty: The seed interface invites early expressions, not necessarily reviewed, adopted, maintained, or actionable contributions.

data.title: A shared library becomes a commons when it is publicly accessible
data.claim: A shared library becomes a commons when it is publicly accessible
data.interpretation: Regen Commons frames a commons as knowledge and work that people collectively use and tend; operational governance still requires evidence.
data.uncertainty: The source itself emphasizes tending and shared practice, while access alone does not establish stewardship, governance, or reciprocity.

data.title: A simulation sandbox predicts real public behavior
data.claim: A simulation sandbox predicts real public behavior
data.interpretation: Treat sandbox results as exploratory evidence and clearly state assumptions, validation limits, and need for real-world review.
data.uncertainty: Synthetic agents and controlled settings may help test hypotheses but cannot fully represent lived political contexts, community histories, or power relations.

data.title: A single accessible format serves all disabled people
data.claim: A single accessible format serves all disabled people
data.interpretation: Provide multiple formats and participation pathways, invite specific needs without forced disclosure, and document unresolved access conflicts.
data.uncertainty: Access needs vary and may conflict across sensory, cognitive, mobility, communication, energy, environmental and other dimensions.

data.title: A Stewardship Council reference proves a formally constituted governing body …
data.claim: A Stewardship Council reference proves a formally constituted governing body exists
data.interpretation: Describe it as a referenced or emerging stewardship body until primary governance records are reviewed.
data.uncertainty: Current forum material references a council but does not by itself establish its membership, mandate, procedures, or authority.

data.title: A successful case provides a transferable best practice
data.claim: A successful case provides a transferable best practice
data.interpretation: Use cases to generate questions, hypotheses and conditional patterns, not universal prescriptions.
data.uncertainty: Case findings arise from specific resources, communities, histories, institutions, technologies and social dilemmas.

data.title: A successful pilot can be scaled by replication
data.claim: A successful pilot can be scaled by replication
data.interpretation: Treat replication as adaptation and institution building, not template copying.
data.uncertainty: Community networks depend on local institutions, policy, terrain, economics, trust and technical capacity.

data.title: A successful school model can be replicated across territories
data.claim: A successful school model can be replicated across territories
data.interpretation: Transfer principles and questions, not a standardized institutional package.
data.uncertainty: Each school is embedded in distinct land histories, movements, climates, political economies and knowledge systems.

data.title: A successful single pilot proves the workflow is inclusive
data.claim: A successful single pilot proves the workflow is inclusive
data.interpretation: Treat one pilot as bounded implementation evidence and repeat with different contributors and tasks before broader claims.
data.uncertainty: One participant and one task cannot represent varied disability, language, class, cultural, caregiving or technological contexts.

data.title: A successful small merge pilot proves the full database can be merged automat…
data.claim: A successful small merge pilot proves the full database can be merged automatically
data.interpretation: Treat the pilot as validation of a method, not proof of database-wide automation readiness.
data.uncertainty: The pilot involved a bounded cluster and still required multiple reviewer roles and unresolved decisions.

data.title: A systems map is an objective representation of reality
data.claim: A systems map is an objective representation of reality
data.interpretation: Treat maps and models as explicit hypotheses that must show assumptions, authorship, omissions and revision history.
data.uncertainty: Boundaries, variables, causal links, time horizons and omitted actors reflect choices and power.

data.title: A talk or panel is reviewed research
data.claim: A talk or panel is reviewed research
data.interpretation: Route talks as media artifacts, claim candidates, concept leads, and implementation prompts; do not treat them as reviewed findings by default.
data.uncertainty: Conference discourse can surface important hypotheses and implementation knowledge but usually lacks peer review or systematic evidence.

data.title: A thinker graph proves direct influence or agreement
data.claim: A thinker graph proves direct influence or agreement
data.interpretation: Record only source-supported relationships and label interpretive connections as analyst synthesis.
data.uncertainty: Conceptual similarity, shared organizations, citations, and later synthesis are different relationship types.

data.title: A thinker’s inclusion means the Toolkit endorses the thinker’s entire body of…
data.claim: A thinker’s inclusion means the Toolkit endorses the thinker’s entire body of work
data.interpretation: State why each thinker matters, which works and concepts are relevant, and what critiques or limits should accompany the lens.
data.uncertainty: Thinker records are navigational and critical nodes, not rankings, heroes, or blanket endorsements.

data.title: A UN complaint independently verifies every incident
data.claim: A UN complaint independently verifies every incident
data.interpretation: Label organizer-reported, legal-submission and independently verified evidence distinctly.
data.uncertainty: International complaints are important advocacy records but still require source attribution and careful incident-level verification.

data.title: A women-led organization automatically distributes power equitably
data.claim: A women-led organization automatically distributes power equitably
data.interpretation: Name the women-led structure while keeping internal governance and representation as review questions.
data.uncertainty: Women’s autonomous infrastructure is significant, but public sources do not fully show internal regional, class, ethnic, age or labor-status power distribution.

data.title: Accelerator graduation means a participatory program succeeded
data.claim: Accelerator graduation means a participatory program succeeded
data.interpretation: Treat completion, grants, and launch as milestones; separately document implementation and outcomes.
data.uncertainty: The program develops action plans and may support pilots, but durability, inclusion, policy influence, and outcomes occur later.

data.title: Access requests require medical proof or diagnostic disclosure
data.claim: Access requests require medical proof or diagnostic disclosure
data.interpretation: Collect only the minimum information needed to provide access; do not require diagnosis unless legally unavoidable and justified.
data.uncertainty: Documentation requirements can create forced intimacy, gatekeeping, delay, cost and exclusion.

data.title: Accessibility belongs to a disability reviewer
data.claim: Accessibility belongs to a disability reviewer
data.interpretation: Assign distributed ownership, budget and backup while preserving disabled-led authority and compensation.
data.uncertainty: Delegating all access labor to one disabled person reproduces unpaid labor and limits organizational responsibility.

data.title: Accessibility can be completed before publication
data.claim: Accessibility can be completed before publication
data.interpretation: Treat accessibility as recurring maintenance with owners, budgets, issue response and review cadence.
data.uncertainty: Access needs, technologies, contributors and content change over time.

data.title: Accessibility can be handled as a final interface checklist
data.claim: Accessibility can be handled as a final interface checklist
data.interpretation: Treat accessibility and disability justice as design and governance concerns throughout the lifecycle.
data.uncertainty: Access needs shape goals, formats, timing, labor, governance and resource allocation from the beginning.

data.title: Accessibility can be handled as a late compliance check
data.claim: Accessibility can be handled as a late compliance check
data.interpretation: Integrate accessibility and disability-led review throughout design, not only before publication.
data.uncertainty: Access needs shape problem framing, participation, interfaces, timing, communication and governance from the beginning.

data.title: Accessibility compliance equals disability justice
data.claim: Accessibility compliance equals disability justice
data.interpretation: Describe compliance precisely and separately assess disability-justice governance and affected-community power.
data.uncertainty: Technical standards and legal compliance can improve access but do not address leadership, race, gender, labor, poverty, institutional power, care or collective liberation.

data.title: Accessible AI is achieved through readable outputs
data.claim: Accessible AI is achieved through readable outputs
data.interpretation: Assess interface access, data rights, use-case legitimacy, governance, labor and remediation together.
data.uncertainty: Readable interfaces do not resolve disability inference, harmful use cases, biased classifications, surveillance or lack of refusal rights.

data.title: Adding provenance metadata makes Indigenous data use ethical
data.claim: Adding provenance metadata makes Indigenous data use ethical
data.interpretation: Provenance is one requirement within a broader governance and relationship process.
data.uncertainty: Provenance improves visibility but cannot establish consent, benefit, authority, reciprocity or appropriate purpose.

data.title: Additional records do not automatically improve usefulness or trustworthiness.
data.claim: Additional records do not automatically improve usefulness or trustworthiness.
data.interpretation: Database-wide
data.uncertainty: Scope Freeze and Backlog
data.context: Require a documented structural gap or user-driven need before reopening expansion.

data.title: African evidence can be generalized continent-wide
data.claim: African evidence can be generalized continent-wide
data.interpretation: Preserve country, method, date and population scope for every claim and comparison.
data.uncertainty: Countries, regions, communities, institutions and infrastructures differ substantially.

data.title: Agroecology can strengthen food sovereignty and climate resilience in Puerto …
data.claim: Agroecology can strengthen food sovereignty and climate resilience in Puerto Rico
data.interpretation: Describe this as a plausible and context-supported contribution, not island-scale proof of food security or quantified resilience.
data.uncertainty: Movement and farm reporting documents diversified ecological practice, farmer networks and disaster recovery.

data.title: Agroecology inherently produces better social and ecological outcomes
data.claim: Agroecology inherently produces better social and ecological outcomes
data.interpretation: Document practices, baselines, ecological evidence, livelihoods, labor, land tenure and affected-party experience for each case.
data.uncertainty: Movement agroecology offers a systemic pathway, but outcomes remain context-, scale-, practice- and power-dependent.

data.title: Agroecology is a neutral technical package
data.claim: Agroecology is a neutral technical package
data.interpretation: Specify whether a source means peasant agroecology, academic agroecology, organic production, climate-smart agriculture or another approach.
data.uncertainty: Movement agroecology includes territory, rights, knowledge, gender, political economy and resistance to corporate capture.

data.title: AI and computational tools can scale participation without sacrificing quality
data.claim: AI and computational tools can scale participation without sacrificing quality
data.interpretation: Evaluate each use across reach, quality, institutional impact, transparency, contestability and human oversight.
data.uncertainty: Tools may support translation, clustering, summarization and coordination, but can also obscure assumptions, amplify bias and weaken deliberative judgment.

data.title: AI assistance can solve the maintenance burden
data.claim: AI assistance can solve the maintenance burden
data.interpretation: Use AI for bounded assistance with logged provenance and human review; fund human maintenance and domain expertise.
data.uncertainty: Automation can identify links, changes, duplicates, and drafts but cannot replace accountable judgment, context, consent, or stewardship.

data.title: AI-assisted deduplication can resolve the merge automatically
data.claim: AI-assisted deduplication can resolve the merge automatically
data.interpretation: Use AI for candidate generation and drafting; require human review for canonical identity, conflicts, sensitivity, and public use.
data.uncertainty: AI can surface candidates and draft syntheses but can collapse distinct entities or invent relationships.

data.title: AI-assisted grant applications
data.claim: AI-assisted grant applications
data.interpretation: Disclose AI assistance, provide non-AI alternatives, preserve applicant control, and evaluate substance rather than writing polish.
data.uncertainty: Applicants may be differently able to use AI, and generated phrasing can influence evaluation or obscure authorship.

data.title: AI-Assisted Is Not Human-Reviewed
data.claim: AI-Assisted Is Not Human-Reviewed
data.uncertainty: Public-use ready as cautionary principle with caveats; do not treat as fully externally reviewed framework.
data.notes: Priority: AI-assisted extraction, classification, summarization, routing, or synthesis should not be treated as human-reviewed knowledge. data.claim: AI-assisted is not human-reviewed
data.uncertainty: Do not publish as fact without status/caveats.

data.title: AI can independently run structural-integrity review
data.claim: AI can independently run structural-integrity review
data.interpretation: Treat AI outputs as review aids requiring source access, human judgment and explicit uncertainty.
data.uncertainty: Prompted AI can surface questions and patterns but may hallucinate, misread context, reproduce power and overstate conformance.

data.title: AI can scale democratic deliberation
data.claim: AI can scale democratic deliberation
data.interpretation: AI may support several dimensions of deliberation; it does not replace civic infrastructure, institutionalization, or human judgment.
data.uncertainty: AI may support translation, facilitation, sensemaking, communication, or setup, but scaling also depends on civic infrastructure, institutions, power, and quality.

data.title: AI fairness metrics can resolve disability exclusion
data.claim: AI fairness metrics can resolve disability exclusion
data.interpretation: Use disability-led justice review, use-case legitimacy, data minimization, subgroup analysis and refusal options in addition to technical metrics.
data.uncertainty: Disability is heterogeneous, contextual and often absent or distorted in datasets; equalized metrics can preserve harmful uses and medicalized assumptions.

data.title: AI-generated agroecology guidance is safe because sources are movement-aligned
data.claim: AI-generated agroecology guidance is safe because sources are movement-aligned
data.interpretation: Treat outputs as cited educational support, not individualized agronomic or safety advice, unless validated for the context.
data.uncertainty: Agricultural decisions are place-specific and can affect livelihoods, soils, water, health and ecological systems; retrieval and generation can still fail.

data.title: AI-mediated knowledge infrastructure can represent a community accurately
data.claim: AI-mediated knowledge infrastructure can represent a community accurately
data.interpretation: KOI Pond is an experiment in contextual and interoperable knowledge organization; accuracy, consent, privacy, plurality, and authority require ongoing human governance.
data.uncertainty: Graph structure and LLM access may omit, distort, expose, or over-authorize community knowledge.

data.title: AI only assists neutral clerical work
data.claim: AI only assists neutral clerical work
data.interpretation: Record consequential AI involvement, affected fields, reviewer, uncertainty, and correction path.
data.uncertainty: Discovery, summarization, classification, prioritization, and duplicate suggestions shape visibility, ontology, and reviewer attention.

data.title: AI or LLM analysis improves deliberation by default
data.claim: AI or LLM analysis improves deliberation by default
data.interpretation: Disclose models, prompts, validation, human review, uncertainty, corrections, and non-AI pathways when AI assists deliberation.
data.uncertainty: Automated summarization or analysis can obscure minority views, introduce errors, or shape facilitation without accountable explanation.
data.context: vTaiwan Democratic Input to AI / Polis

data.title: AI training on publicly accessible Indigenous material is automatically permi…
data.claim: AI training on publicly accessible Indigenous material is automatically permissible
data.interpretation: Require Indigenous data-governance review, provenance and community-specific permissions before AI ingestion or model use.
data.uncertainty: Public accessibility does not establish authority, appropriate purpose, collective benefit or ethical reuse in AI systems.

data.title: An access checklist can substitute for relationship and adaptation
data.claim: An access checklist can substitute for relationship and adaptation
data.interpretation: Use standards as minimums and maintain revisable protocols, feedback, repair and disabled-led governance.
data.uncertainty: Checklists can establish baselines but may freeze assumptions and ignore changing contexts, power and lived experience.

data.title: An AI Donation Agent objectively allocates to the highest-impact projects
data.claim: An AI Donation Agent objectively allocates to the highest-impact projects
data.interpretation: Giveth Causes uses an AI-assisted allocation process; its criteria, data, oversight and limitations should be visible and challengeable.
data.uncertainty: Model criteria, data quality, curator choices and project visibility influence allocations.

data.title: An alias list is sufficient for identity resolution
data.claim: An alias list is sufficient for identity resolution
data.interpretation: Store aliases as sourced, typed, dated records.
data.uncertainty: Handles, translations, legal names, historic labels, and abbreviations have different scopes and validity.

data.title: An initiative documented as an alternative has been validated as transformative
data.claim: An initiative documented as an alternative has been validated as transformative
data.interpretation: Describe the initiative, source and context; preserve self-assessment and seek affected-party and outcome evidence before broader claims.
data.uncertainty: Documentation, network inclusion or self-description can surface valuable practices but does not independently establish outcomes, justice or transferability.

data.title: ANAMURI represents one unified rural-women perspective
data.claim: ANAMURI represents one unified rural-women perspective
data.interpretation: Describe the specific constituency, territory, process and date behind each claim; do not treat umbrella statements as unanimous consent.
data.uncertainty: Its umbrella includes Indigenous women, wage workers, producers, fishers, youth and geographically diverse organizations whose interests and authority may differ.

data.title: Anti-colonial methods can be copied as a universal checklist
data.claim: Anti-colonial methods can be copied as a universal checklist
data.interpretation: Treat methods as situated practices requiring community-defined adaptation and refusal rights.
data.uncertainty: Relational methods depend on land, history, authority, accountability and local protocols.

data.title: Anyone may apply or customize TK and BC Labels
data.claim: Anyone may apply or customize TK and BC Labels
data.interpretation: Only represent a Label when it is linked to the community-controlled Local Contexts project or source.
data.uncertainty: Labels express Indigenous community authority and are designed for customization and application by communities.

data.title: API-accessible participatory data is safe for unrestricted reuse
data.claim: API-accessible participatory data is safe for unrestricted reuse
data.interpretation: Apply data minimization, purpose limits and contextual-integrity review.
data.uncertainty: Access can enable profiling, aggregation or reuse outside participant expectations.

data.title: Assembly participation is not decision power
data.claim: Assembly participation is not decision power
data.interpretation: Trace proposals, delegates, voting/consensus rules and follow-through.
data.uncertainty: Women, youth and diversity assemblies can surface agendas without guaranteeing influence on final congress decisions.

data.title: Audrey Tang created or represents g0v
data.claim: Audrey Tang created or represents g0v
data.interpretation: Describe Tang's documented roles and contributions while preserving g0v's collective and decentralized identity.
data.uncertainty: g0v explicitly describes itself as polycentric, autonomous and without a single representative; Tang is one contributor and bridge figure among many.

data.title: Automated accessibility checks establish public readiness
data.claim: Automated accessibility checks establish public readiness
data.interpretation: Use automated checks as one input alongside manual and disabled-led testing.
data.uncertainty: Automated tools miss context, cognitive barriers, screen-reader usability, access conflicts and structural exclusion.

data.title: Automated digests represent the state of the ecosystem
data.claim: Automated digests represent the state of the ecosystem
data.interpretation: Regen Heartbeat provides an automated, source-dependent view of selected ecosystem activity and should remain correctable and transparent about coverage.
data.uncertainty: A digest reflects selected sources, ranking logic, prompts, and publication cadence rather than the whole ecosystem.

data.claim: Better knowledge governance proves better material or ecological outcomes

data.interpretation: Representation is one dimension; assess who leads, benefits, owns, decides and bears risk across the design process.

data.title: Bioregional intelligence and local sovereignty
data.claim: Bioregional intelligence and local sovereignty
data.interpretation: Require local governance, consent, benefit sharing, access controls, and the ability to correct, withdraw, or restrict knowledge.

data.title: Broadcasts and network reports
data.claim: Broadcasts and network reports
data.interpretation: Treat as first-party source material and implementation leads; distinguish stated activity, interpretation, outputs, and independently supported outcomes.
data.uncertainty: Reports and retrospectives are primarily network-authored field memory.

data.title: Calling the Toolkit a commons means contributors already share meaningful power
data.claim: Calling the Toolkit a commons means contributors already share meaningful power
data.interpretation: Describe current decision rights honestly and distinguish aspirational commons governance from implemented contributor authority.

data.title: Care and coordination work can be handled through goodwill
data.claim: Care and coordination work can be handled through goodwill
data.interpretation: Name care and coordination roles, support them materially, and avoid concentrating them invisibly in a few people.
data.uncertainty: Onboarding, facilitation, conflict mediation, accessibility support, and relationship maintenance require time, skill, boundaries, and often compensation.

data.title: Care-centered governance is free of conflict or coercion
data.claim: Care-centered governance is free of conflict or coercion
data.interpretation: Preserve autonomy, appeals, boundaries, plural practices and explicit power review.

data.claim: Care data should be collected to improve support
data.interpretation: Collect the minimum necessary information, allow low-disclosure requests, separate support from evaluation, and restrict access.
data.uncertainty: Care needs, disability, family responsibilities and crisis information can be highly sensitive.

data.title: Care language proves a system is caring
data.claim: Care language proves a system is caring
data.interpretation: Treat care as a claim requiring evidence about resources, workload, authority, competence, feedback and outcomes.

data.interpretation: Use principles and tools to support community authority; do not substitute schemas for governance relationships.

data.claim: Care practices can replace compensation and institutional support

data.claim: Care webs eliminate burnout
data.interpretation: Evaluate boundaries, compensation, backup capacity, repair and the ability to reduce or stop work.
data.uncertainty: Distributed support can improve resilience but still fail under scarcity, conflict or chronic overload.

data.title: Centralizing movement knowledge in an assistant necessarily democratizes access
data.claim: Centralizing movement knowledge in an assistant necessarily democratizes access
data.interpretation: Evaluate whether the system preserves plurality, local authority, dissent, source context and routes back to people and organizations.
data.uncertainty: Centralization can improve discovery while also concentrating classification power, erasing disagreements or weakening local knowledge relationships.

data.title: Children’s participation requires heightened safeguards
data.claim: Children’s participation requires heightened safeguards
data.interpretation: Use child-safe consent, minimal data and no sensitive participant-level extraction.
data.uncertainty: Documentation of children’s movement spaces can expose identities, locations and political affiliations.

data.title: Claim Is Not Evidence
data.claim: Claim Is Not Evidence
data.uncertainty: Public-use ready as cautionary principle with caveats; do not treat as fully externally reviewed framework.
data.notes: Priority: A claim can be useful, source-linked, important, inspiring, or worth preserving without being treated as evidence. Claims should be preserved for review; they are not treated as evidence by default. · Next: Add as core structural integrity principle; link to related guardrail claims; use as baseline rule for future claim candidates. · Notes: Added in Batch 1A Claims update.
data.review_needs: Discovery_Pool promotion — verify claim + evidence

data.title: Claim is not evidence
data.claim: Claim is not evidence
data.uncertainty: Do not publish as fact without status/caveats.
data.notes: Priority: Core claim-evidence discipline. · Next: Keep visible as protective claim; link to evidence/source context. · Notes: Integrity-protecting claim.
data.review_needs: Discovery_Pool promotion — verify claim + evidence

data.title: Collecting care and workload data automatically improves wellbeing
data.claim: Collecting care and workload data automatically improves wellbeing
data.interpretation: Collect only decision-relevant information with consent, access limits and deletion rules.
data.uncertainty: Data collection can create surveillance, stigma, managerial pressure or forced disclosure.

data.title: Collecting more accommodation detail produces better access
data.claim: Collecting more accommodation detail produces better access
data.interpretation: Collect only what is operationally necessary; support changing needs without diagnosis or repeated justification.
data.uncertainty: Detailed records may create forced disclosure, privacy risks and a hidden disability dataset.

data.title: Collective construction and volunteer work are inherently emancipatory
data.claim: Collective construction and volunteer work are inherently emancipatory
data.interpretation: Document authority, voluntariness, compensation, care, accessibility, safety and who performs maintenance.
data.uncertainty: Mutirão and solidarity labor may build ownership and capacity while also creating unequal, gendered or unpaid burdens.

data.title: Combining governance source systems creates one coherent governance model
data.claim: Combining governance source systems creates one coherent governance model
data.interpretation: Treat the batch as a plural source portfolio with explicit tensions, not a unified doctrine.
data.uncertainty: The selected systems differ in epistemology, constituency, institutional mandate, scale and political context.

data.title: Combining research, cases, training and tools creates a complete participatio…
data.claim: Combining research, cases, training and tools creates a complete participation system
data.interpretation: The systems can inform a modular support environment; each deployment still requires local governance and affected-party review.
data.uncertainty: The six systems cover complementary functions, but composition does not eliminate politics, exclusion, conflict or maintenance burdens.

data.title: Combining several respected thinkers produces a complete or neutral framework
data.claim: Combining several respected thinkers produces a complete or neutral framework
data.interpretation: Use them as complementary and contestable review lenses; preserve tensions and add missing perspectives.
data.uncertainty: The clusters have different normative commitments, evidence bases, domains, and blind spots.

data.title: Common identifiers make records directly comparable
data.claim: Common identifiers make records directly comparable
data.interpretation: Use identifiers for connection, then preserve each source system’s method, scope and uncertainty.
data.uncertainty: Shared identifiers improve linking but do not harmonize definitions, methods, time windows or claims.

data.title: Commoner credentials are a neutral way to protect shared infrastructure
data.claim: Commoner credentials are a neutral way to protect shared infrastructure
data.interpretation: Treat credentialed access as an option requiring privacy, accessibility, governance, and appeal review.
data.uncertainty: Credentials and conditional access may protect reciprocity but can also create exclusion, surveillance, lock-in, or centralized gatekeeping.

data.title: Commons-based peer production replaces markets and states
data.claim: Commons-based peer production replaces markets and states
data.interpretation: Commons-transition work proposes rebalancing and transforming institutional roles; actual arrangements are mixed and context-dependent.
data.uncertainty: Most proposals describe transformed relationships among commons, markets, and public institutions rather than simple replacement.

data.title: Commons language guarantees shared benefit
data.claim: Commons language guarantees shared benefit
data.interpretation: Identify who contributes, governs, benefits, bears costs, and can contest decisions.
data.uncertainty: Commons can exclude, burden maintainers, reproduce hierarchy, or distribute benefits unevenly.

data.title: Commons naturally distribute care fairly
data.claim: Commons naturally distribute care fairly
data.interpretation: Commons may support collective reproduction, but care burdens and authority must be examined directly.
data.uncertainty: Commons can reproduce patriarchy, exclusion, unpaid labor and unequal access without explicit governance.

data.title: Communication visibility ≠ editorial centralization
data.claim: Communication visibility ≠ editorial centralization
data.interpretation: Map media, teams and archives by territory and artifact; do not infer one editorial chain.
data.uncertainty: The official site and named communicators are only part of a distributed territorial media ecosystem.

data.title: Community-centered alternatives are inherently inclusive
data.claim: Community-centered alternatives are inherently inclusive
data.interpretation: Review who defines the community, who participates, who benefits, who bears burdens and who can dissent or leave.
data.uncertainty: Communities contain differences and power inequalities involving caste, gender, class, disability, age, ethnicity and other structures.

data.title: Community-driven AI is inherently just
data.claim: Community-driven AI is inherently just
data.interpretation: Assess authority, purpose, harms, labor, data rights, maintenance and institutional context for each prototype.
data.uncertainty: Community participation can coexist with unsafe use cases, unequal labor, weak consent or external infrastructure dependence.

data.title: Community economies language means all economic practices are benign
data.claim: Community economies language means all economic practices are benign
data.interpretation: Use the lens to broaden visibility while still assessing power, harm and distribution.
data.uncertainty: Economic diversity includes exploitative, coerced and ecologically damaging relations as well as alternatives.

data.title: Community Funds democratize funding decisions
data.claim: Community Funds democratize funding decisions
data.interpretation: Artizen Community Funds enable community-led curation within platform rules; the distribution of power, representation, and accountability should be assessed per Fund.
data.uncertainty: Community curation may broaden participation, but fund creation and curation can still concentrate authority in visible or well-connected stewards.

data.title: Community land ownership automatically creates community control
data.claim: Community land ownership automatically creates community control
data.interpretation: Record board composition, decision rights, ground-lease terms, affordability formulas and affected-party evidence.
data.uncertainty: Formal land ownership can coexist with weak resident power, inaccessible governance or exclusionary rules.

data.title: Community network means community-controlled
data.claim: Community network means community-controlled
data.interpretation: Verify legal ownership, operational authority, governance, labor, benefit distribution and exit rights.
data.uncertainty: Projects may use community branding while ownership, decisions, technical power or revenue remain external.

data.title: Community network means community controlled
data.claim: Community network means community controlled
data.interpretation: Describe the specific governance, ownership, operational and decision rights held by community members.
data.uncertainty: Projects may use community language while ownership, licensing, technical decisions, funding or data remain externally controlled.

data.title: Community-owned infrastructure produces better social outcomes
data.claim: Community-owned infrastructure produces better social outcomes
data.interpretation: Community ownership is an important institutional variable; evaluate outcomes and tradeoffs case by case.
data.uncertainty: Cooperative or community ownership can improve relevance and agency, but outcomes depend on governance, affordability, capacity, regulation, maintenance and local conditions.

data.title: Community participation in data collection transfers decision authority
data.claim: Community participation in data collection transfers decision authority
data.interpretation: State who controls questions, data, categories, interpretation, release and future reuse.
data.uncertainty: People may contribute stories or annotations while institutions retain ownership, framing, analysis and publication control.

data.title: Community participation means community control
data.claim: Community participation means community control
data.interpretation: State the community’s actual decision rights, compensation, ownership, refusal options and continuing governance.
data.uncertainty: People may be consulted or invited without controlling scope, resources, decisions, ownership or whether a project proceeds.

data.title: Community-situated research artifacts can be generalized across contexts
data.claim: Community-situated research artifacts can be generalized across contexts
data.interpretation: Preserve the original community context and treat cross-context reuse as a new adaptation requiring affected-party review.
data.uncertainty: Artifacts were created with particular communities, histories, risks, languages, and governance relationships.

data.title: Conference webpages are reliable archival records
data.claim: Conference webpages are reliable archival records
data.interpretation: Use event pages as source leads, preserve dates and screenshots where needed, and verify important details through recordings, agendas, repositories, and partner sources.
data.uncertainty: Several current pages contain incomplete agendas, placeholder testimonials, template fragments, or legacy content alongside useful program information.

data.title: Configuring democratic features guarantees democratic outcomes
data.claim: Configuring democratic features guarantees democratic outcomes
data.interpretation: Describe Decidim as configurable infrastructure; evaluate democratic quality at process and institutional levels.
data.uncertainty: Authority, inclusion, facilitation, recruitment and institutional follow-through remain outside the software.

data.title: Congress declarations prove implementation
data.claim: Congress declarations prove implementation
data.interpretation: Record declarations as governance and learning artifacts, then separately trace decisions, resources and follow-through.
data.uncertainty: Congress outputs establish agendas and public commitments, not completed policy, budget allocation or territorial outcomes.

data.title: Connectivity automatically empowers communities
data.claim: Connectivity automatically empowers communities
data.interpretation: Describe the infrastructure, community authority, uses, burdens and outcomes separately.
data.uncertainty: Connectivity can increase surveillance, dependency, cost, harassment or extraction when governance and local benefit are weak.

data.title: Connectivity is inherently empowering
data.claim: Connectivity is inherently empowering
data.interpretation: Assess connectivity alongside community goals, ownership, governance, safety, cultural fit, ecological effects and the right to refuse.
data.uncertainty: Connectivity can support rights and livelihoods but can also introduce surveillance, extraction, platform dependency, misinformation and unwanted social change.

data.title: Consensus mapping identifies the public will
data.claim: Consensus mapping identifies the public will
data.interpretation: Describe the participant population, process, algorithmic role, facilitation and policy pathway before making consensus claims.
data.uncertainty: Opinion clusters and areas of agreement depend on participant recruitment, statement generation, moderation, algorithm design and institutional use.

data.title: Consensus signals represent the public will
data.claim: Consensus signals represent the public will
data.interpretation: Describe the participant population, process and analytical method; treat consensus as a bounded process signal.
data.uncertainty: Opinion groups and cross-group agreement depend on recruitment, framing, moderation, statement supply and analytic choices.

data.title: Consensus statements are neutral outputs
data.claim: Consensus statements are neutral outputs
data.interpretation: Publish how consensus statements were generated and retain disagreement, uncertainty, and excluded statements in the record.
data.uncertainty: Consensus depends on which statements appear, moderation rules, outreach, participation, and thresholds or analytic choices.

data.title: Consent settings fully resolve community-data governance
data.claim: Consent settings fully resolve community-data governance
data.interpretation: Treat consent controls as one governance layer alongside purpose limitation, community rules, correction, deletion, and review.
data.uncertainty: Individual opt-outs do not alone address collective context, inferred relationships, downstream synthesis, power, or future reuse.

data.title: Constituency space ≠ equitable power
data.claim: Constituency space ≠ equitable power
data.interpretation: Review rules-in-use, resources, outcomes and confidential participant perspectives.
data.uncertainty: Assemblies, schools and collectives show organization but not necessarily budget power, agenda control or safety.

data.title: Consultation gives contributors meaningful authority
data.claim: Consultation gives contributors meaningful authority
data.interpretation: State the exact decisions contributors can make, contest or veto and where authority remains elsewhere.
data.uncertainty: Participants may be heard while others retain all editorial, classification and publication power.

data.title: Continental scale is not uniform authority
data.claim: Continental scale is not uniform authority
data.interpretation: Record region, constituency, member organization, date and decision scope separately.
data.uncertainty: A large network and congress do not imply that every organization or constituency holds equal agenda-setting power.

data.title: Contribution credits fairly measure value
data.claim: Contribution credits fairly measure value
data.interpretation: Treat credits as one governance input and preserve qualitative review, appeals and non-measured contributions.
data.uncertainty: Quantitative contribution recognition can exclude care, invisible labor, dissent, low-volume expertise and structurally marginalized contributors.

data.title: Contributor metrics improve accountability without risk
data.claim: Contributor metrics improve accountability without risk
data.interpretation: Minimize contributor data, prohibit covert ranking, and use aggregate or qualitative signals with contributor governance.
data.uncertainty: Activity counts can become hidden performance scoring, incentivize volume, and expose sensitive participation patterns.

data.title: COOPAC is formally governed by UNICRAB
data.claim: COOPAC is formally governed by UNICRAB
data.interpretation: Record the relationship as a lead until membership or governance documentation is confirmed.
data.uncertainty: The public sources place COOPAC in the agrarian-reform cooperative ecosystem but do not clearly establish formal affiliation or authority.

data.title: COOPAC/Nutrilê strengthens regional development and family-farm income
data.claim: COOPAC/Nutrilê strengthens regional development and family-farm income
data.interpretation: The chain is intended to strengthen regional processing, markets and producer income; realized effects require follow-up.
data.uncertainty: This is a plausible and organizer-stated pathway, but household-level and distributional evidence is limited.

data.title: Cooperative and association counts prove democratic ownership or improved liv…
data.claim: Cooperative and association counts prove democratic ownership or improved livelihoods
data.interpretation: Document each cooperative’s governance, membership, labor, finances and outcomes separately.
data.uncertainty: Legal form and scale do not establish rules-in-use, worker power, income distribution, gender equity or durability.

data.title: Cooperative form automatically produces racial or economic justice
data.claim: Cooperative form automatically produces racial or economic justice
data.interpretation: Assess history, constituency, governance, capital, labor and benefit distribution.
data.uncertainty: Legal form alone does not establish member power, reparative effects, access or equitable distribution.

data.title: Cooperative legal form proves democratic control
data.claim: Cooperative legal form proves democratic control
data.interpretation: Review rules-in-use, member participation, decisions, revenue, work and community perspectives.
data.uncertainty: Formal structure may not reveal participation quality, power concentration, labor burdens or who benefits.

data.title: Cooperative registration proves democratic member control
data.claim: Cooperative registration proves democratic member control
data.interpretation: Describe cooperative form separately from reviewed rules-in-use and member experience.
data.uncertainty: Legal form and collective origin do not establish actual voting, transparency, equitable voice or grievance handling.

data.title: Correction mechanisms are enough without preserving disagreement
data.claim: Correction mechanisms are enough without preserving disagreement
data.interpretation: Allow contested status, multiple perspectives, unresolved questions, and visible decision history.
data.uncertainty: Some disputes cannot be conclusively resolved, and a single corrected record may erase legitimate plurality or power asymmetry.

data.title: Cosmo-local production reduces ecological impact
data.claim: Cosmo-local production reduces ecological impact
data.interpretation: Cosmo-local approaches aim to align global knowledge with local production; ecological effects require lifecycle and supply-chain evidence.
data.uncertainty: Global knowledge sharing and local production may reduce some transport or duplication but can also increase energy use, material demand, and fragmented production.

data.title: CRAFT makes evaluation claims reliable
data.claim: CRAFT makes evaluation claims reliable
data.interpretation: CRAFT offers a meta-standard for specifying auditable evaluation chains; reliability still requires correct domain application and testing.
data.uncertainty: CRAFT specifies conditions for a reliable evaluation chain but does not itself validate an implementation or its domain assumptions.

data.title: Creative Commons content can be freely reused for any purpose
data.claim: Creative Commons content can be freely reused for any purpose
data.interpretation: Preserve attribution and license metadata and review intended reuse against the license before publication or product integration.
data.uncertainty: The site uses CC BY-NC-SA 3.0, which includes attribution, noncommercial, and ShareAlike requirements.

data.title: Creator and project claims
data.claim: Creator and project claims
data.interpretation: Preserve attribution; separate project claims from independent evidence and outcomes.
data.uncertainty: Project pages are often self-descriptions and fundraising narratives.

data.title: Critical-data frameworks can be merged into one generic responsible-AI checklist
data.claim: Critical-data frameworks can be merged into one generic responsible-AI checklist
data.interpretation: Preserve source-specific authority and questions; compose lenses without erasing differences or substituting one for another.
data.uncertainty: Data Feminism, Design Justice, CARE, Local Contexts, Race After Technology and AJL arise from distinct lineages, communities and claims.

data.title: Cross-platform project identity
data.claim: Cross-platform project identity
data.interpretation: Preserve mapping provenance, dates and confidence; do not merge identities only because names appear similar.
data.uncertainty: The same project may use different names, repositories, wallets, fiscal hosts or organizational boundaries across systems.

data.title: CROSS reporting proves public-goods outcomes
data.claim: CROSS reporting proves public-goods outcomes
data.interpretation: Use CROSS to clarify obligations and evidence expectations; evaluate outcomes through domain evidence and affected-party review.
data.uncertainty: Obligation and reporting architecture can improve legibility without establishing causality, quality, justice or long-term outcomes.

data.title: Crowdsourcing can produce high-quality comparative social-science data
data.claim: Crowdsourcing can produce high-quality comparative social-science data
data.interpretation: Participedia is an important experiment in structured crowdsourced comparative data; quality should be assessed field by field and use by use.
data.uncertainty: Structured forms, editorial tending, codebooks, and contributor histories can improve quality, but uneven participation and review constrain inference.

data.title: Cultural and place-based artifacts
data.claim: Cultural and place-based artifacts
data.interpretation: Review consent, cultural authority, privacy, location sensitivity, attribution, revocation, and benefit sharing before treating artifacts as reusable commons material.
data.uncertainty: Projects may tokenize, archive, geolocate, or commercialize stories, artworks, ecological narratives, and community memory.

data.title: Current-state handoff means labor and provenance conditions can be omitted
data.claim: Current-state handoff means labor and provenance conditions can be omitted
data.interpretation: Keep the public artifact current-state focused while including concise stewardship, workload and support requirements.
data.uncertainty: A singular version can still conceal who must maintain it and under what conditions.

data.title: DAO metadata interoperability establishes governance transparency
data.claim: DAO metadata interoperability establishes governance transparency
data.interpretation: DAOstar and EIP-4824 support common metadata and discoverability; they do not certify transparent or legitimate governance.
data.uncertainty: Shared metadata can improve discovery but may not reveal actual power, informal influence, conflicts, or decision quality.

data.title: Data are neutral observations waiting to be analyzed
data.claim: Data are neutral observations waiting to be analyzed
data.interpretation: Describe who produced the data, for what purpose, under what conditions, and what remains missing or contested.
data.uncertainty: Data reflect collection choices, institutional priorities, categories, omissions, labor and unequal social relations.

data.title: Data-as-soil framing guarantees regenerative data governance
data.claim: Data-as-soil framing guarantees regenerative data governance
data.interpretation: Use the metaphor as a prompt and require explicit data-governance rules and affected-party review.
data.uncertainty: A relational metaphor does not itself define ownership, consent, access, deletion, security, compensation or public authority.

data.title: Decidim guarantees democratic participation
data.claim: Decidim guarantees democratic participation
data.interpretation: Decidim provides configurable participatory infrastructure; democratic quality depends on process design, governance, access, facilitation, and follow-through.
data.uncertainty: Software capabilities and democratic principles do not guarantee inclusion, deliberative quality, institutional authority, or implementation.

data.title: Decolonial framing can be inferred from geography or identity
data.claim: Decolonial framing can be inferred from geography or identity
data.interpretation: Use organizations' own stated frameworks and examine how authority, knowledge and benefits are governed in practice.
data.uncertainty: Decolonial practice concerns power, knowledge, land, institutions and relationships; it should not be assigned as a branding label without source support.

data.title: Deep leverage points are automatically easier or more ethical
data.claim: Deep leverage points are automatically easier or more ethical
data.interpretation: Evaluate intervention depth alongside legitimacy, consent, feasibility, reversibility and affected-party power.
data.uncertainty: Changing goals, rules or paradigms may involve coercion, concentrated authority and long political struggle.

data.title: Deferred does not mean unimportant, rejected or lower quality.
data.claim: Deferred does not mean unimportant, rejected or lower quality.
data.interpretation: Governance
data.uncertainty: Scope Freeze and Backlog
data.context: Backlog priority reflects current-version sequencing, evidence readiness and consolidation needs.

data.title: DelibTech Network membership proves a tool or practitioner is effective
data.claim: DelibTech Network membership proves a tool or practitioner is effective
data.interpretation: Record membership as a relationship and participation signal; evaluate tools and practices through separate evidence.
data.uncertainty: The network is a community of practice with invite-only membership, not an accreditation or evaluation system.

data.title: Design can redistribute power toward affected communities
data.claim: Design can redistribute power toward affected communities
data.interpretation: Design justice seeks to shift design authority and benefits toward affected communities; whether power changes must be evaluated in practice.
data.uncertainty: Design processes can change authority and ownership, but outcomes depend on institutions, resources and enforcement.

data.title: Design justice is a neutral facilitation technique
data.claim: Design justice is a neutral facilitation technique
data.interpretation: Present design justice as a values-based framework and disclose where its commitments shape review and decision-making.
data.uncertainty: The framework is explicitly normative and political, focused on structural inequality, collective liberation and ecological survival.

data.title: Developer activity growth proves a grant program created public-goods impact
data.claim: Developer activity growth proves a grant program created public-goods impact
data.interpretation: OSO analyses can show associations between funding and observed software activity; causal and public-value claims require additional design and evidence.
data.uncertainty: Software activity is a useful signal but does not by itself establish causality, quality, maintenance, downstream use or broader public value.

data.title: Digital participation tools make a process inclusive
data.claim: Digital participation tools make a process inclusive
data.interpretation: Assess digital and offline access, privacy, accessibility, recruitment, facilitation, and institutional follow-through together.
data.uncertainty: Digital tools can expand access for some while excluding others through connectivity, literacy, disability, surveillance, language, or trust barriers.

data.title: Digital public infrastructure creates public value
data.claim: Digital public infrastructure creates public value
data.interpretation: Assess DPI through governance, financing, justice, sustainability and affected-user evidence.
data.uncertainty: Technical scale or adoption does not establish inclusion, accountability, rights protection or public benefit.

data.title: Disabled participation means disabled people held design authority
data.claim: Disabled participation means disabled people held design authority
data.interpretation: State the exact role and decision rights of disabled participants and reviewers.
data.uncertainty: Consultation, user testing or attendance can occur without agenda-setting, governance, ownership, compensation or refusal power.

data.title: Diversity visibility can increase exposure
data.claim: Diversity visibility can increase exposure
data.interpretation: Use public professional information only, minimize personal data and enable removal/correction.
data.uncertainty: Public recognition can support dignity and organizing while also increasing personal and territorial security risks.

data.title: Documenting an alternative helps the community that created it
data.claim: Documenting an alternative helps the community that created it
data.interpretation: Track consent, attribution, intended audience, benefits returned, correction rights and visibility preferences.
data.uncertainty: Visibility can produce benefits, but it can also extract stories, expose communities or redirect recognition toward intermediaries.

data.title: Ecocredit issuance or retirement proves regeneration occurred
data.claim: Ecocredit issuance or retirement proves regeneration occurred
data.interpretation: State the methodology, monitoring period, verifier, evidence access, registry event and remaining uncertainties separately.
data.uncertainty: Issuance and retirement are registry events dependent on a methodology and evidence process; they are not self-interpreting proof of ecological or community outcomes.

data.title: Ecocredits are interchangeable measures of regeneration
data.claim: Ecocredits are interchangeable measures of regeneration
data.interpretation: Ecocredits should be interpreted within their credit class, methodology, project, batch, unit, geography, vintage, and supporting evidence.
data.uncertainty: Credits may represent different ecosystem services, units, methodologies, regions, time horizons, safeguards, and evidence standards.

data.title: Ecological claim and evidence separation
data.claim: Ecological claim and evidence separation
data.interpretation: Store claim, evidence, methodology, review stage, verifier, uncertainty, date, and project context as separate fields.
data.uncertainty: Project, protocol, and marketplace pages can combine technical claims, marketing language, registry status, and project self-reporting.

data.title: Embedding and entity-resolution errors
data.claim: Embedding and entity-resolution errors
data.interpretation: Preserve raw source links, versions, transformation logs, confidence, and human correction pathways for normalized and graph records.
data.uncertainty: Semantic processing can merge distinct entities, lose context, or create misleading relationships.

data.title: Energy-justice policy language proves frontline control
data.claim: Energy-justice policy language proves frontline control
data.interpretation: Separate participation, decision power, ownership, labor and material outcomes.
data.uncertainty: Recognition or consultation can coexist with centralized ownership and weak community decision rights.

data.title: ENFF participation counts prove educational outcomes
data.claim: ENFF participation counts prove educational outcomes
data.interpretation: Treat counts as organizer-reported reach and assess outcomes through participant and movement evidence.
data.uncertainty: Numbers trained or hosted do not establish learning quality, power changes, later leadership or territorial impact.

data.title: ENFF participation reach proves political or educational impact
data.claim: ENFF participation reach proves political or educational impact
data.interpretation: State reach as organizer-reported and separately assess curriculum, participant experience, application, exclusions and maintenance.
data.uncertainty: Organizer-reported learner counts establish reach, not learning quality, political outcomes, accessibility or territorial application.

data.title: English summaries preserve the meaning of movement-generated knowledge
data.claim: English summaries preserve the meaning of movement-generated knowledge
data.interpretation: Retain original language, translator and reviewer information, and locally preferred terms wherever possible.
data.uncertainty: Political and cultural concepts can shift substantially through translation and ontology mapping.

data.title: Every merge decision needs every specialist reviewer
data.claim: Every merge decision needs every specialist reviewer
data.interpretation: Use risk-tiered review and reserve specialist review for consequential or public-facing assertions.
data.uncertainty: Uniform review requirements would create bottlenecks and hidden labor while adding little value to low-risk metadata.

data.title: Evidence caution
data.claim: Evidence caution
data.interpretation: Label evidence type consistently.
data.uncertainty: https://cloc-viacampesina.net/
data.context: Reports establish current programs, schools and declarations while usually lacking counterfactual or participant-level evaluation.

data.title: Evidence of impact = Yes establishes impact
data.claim: Evidence of impact = Yes establishes impact
data.interpretation: Treat the field as a lead to inspect the stated evidence and original sources, not as a validated outcome.
data.uncertainty: The field may reflect contributor interpretation and may not specify independence, methodology, magnitude, duration, or affected-party views.

data.title: FAIR or open data is sufficient for responsible Indigenous data governance
data.claim: FAIR or open data is sufficient for responsible Indigenous data governance
data.interpretation: Use FAIR together with CARE and community-specific governance; openness is not the default goal for all data.
data.uncertainty: Findability and reuse can increase extraction or harm when authority, benefit, responsibility and ethics are not addressed.

data.title: Fairness means equal classification accuracy across groups
data.claim: Fairness means equal classification accuracy across groups
data.interpretation: Evaluate whether the system should be used, who bears risk, who can refuse, and what remedies exist.
data.uncertainty: Technical parity can leave coercive, illegitimate or discriminatory systems intact.

data.title: Farmer-to-farmer learning is automatically horizontal and inclusive
data.claim: Farmer-to-farmer learning is automatically horizontal and inclusive
data.interpretation: Document facilitation, participation, authority, compensation and adaptation rather than assuming equality.
data.uncertainty: Gender, age, land access, literacy, language, caste, race and organizational status can still shape whose knowledge travels.

data.title: Farmer-to-farmer learning is automatically horizontal and inclusive
data.claim: Farmer-to-farmer learning is automatically horizontal and inclusive
data.interpretation: Describe the learning design and review actual participation, authority, compensation and adaptation.
data.uncertainty: Informal expertise, gender, age, land access, language and movement status can shape who teaches, speaks and benefits.

data.title: Federation solves the scale problem for local cooperatives
data.claim: Federation solves the scale problem for local cooperatives
data.interpretation: Federation is one strategy for sharing infrastructure while retaining local ownership; its effects require governance and member-level evidence.
data.uncertainty: Shared infrastructure can reduce costs and increase bargaining power, but federation introduces governance, financing, coordination, and uneven-capacity challenges.

data.title: Feminist social reproduction theory is one unified framework
data.claim: Feminist social reproduction theory is one unified framework
data.interpretation: Name the specific lineage and limits of each concept rather than collapsing them into one authoritative theory.
data.uncertainty: The field includes multiple Marxist, Black feminist, Indigenous, decolonial, disability and queer traditions with different emphases.

data.title: First-person disability stories represent the disability community
data.claim: First-person disability stories represent the disability community
data.interpretation: Treat testimony as scoped first-person evidence and preserve plurality, contributor context and non-representativeness.
data.uncertainty: Stories provide essential situated knowledge but disability communities are diverse and structurally unequal.

data.title: Food sovereignty is equivalent to national food self-sufficiency
data.claim: Food sovereignty is equivalent to national food self-sufficiency
data.interpretation: Use the movement’s stated multidimensional definition and preserve debates about trade, states and territorial autonomy.
data.uncertainty: Food sovereignty centers peoples’ democratic control, rights, culture, ecology and producer livelihoods, not isolation or simple domestic production totals.

data.title: Food sovereignty is the same as food security
data.claim: Food sovereignty is the same as food security
data.interpretation: Treat food sovereignty as a political framework centered on peoples' authority over food and agriculture systems, not as a synonym for food security.
data.uncertainty: Food security can focus on availability and access without addressing who controls land, seeds, production, trade and policy.

data.title: Formal governance documents describe actual governance
data.claim: Formal governance documents describe actual governance
data.interpretation: Compare formal rules with observed practices, decision records, participant accounts and technical controls.
data.uncertainty: Rules-in-use, informal norms, technical infrastructure and power may differ from constitutions, policies, licenses or public descriptions.

data.title: Formal governance documents describe how an institution actually works
data.claim: Formal governance documents describe how an institution actually works
data.interpretation: Treat formal rules as one evidence layer and investigate rules-in-use through implementation records and participant perspectives.
data.uncertainty: Formal rules may differ significantly from practiced norms, informal power, enforcement, and exceptions.

data.title: Formal integrity and participatory openness eliminate power
data.claim: Formal integrity and participatory openness eliminate power
data.interpretation: Review formal rules and open processes alongside material power, labor, access, and affected-party experience.
data.uncertainty: Power can operate through agenda setting, expertise, infrastructure ownership, workload, classification, funding, and informal networks.

data.title: Forum discussion equals ratified governance
data.claim: Forum discussion equals ratified governance
data.interpretation: Record authorship, date, proposal status, decision path, and implementation evidence separately.
data.uncertainty: Forum posts, call notes, and proposals preserve valuable field memory but may remain exploratory or contested.

data.title: Founder-centered thinker maps adequately represent a field
data.claim: Founder-centered thinker maps adequately represent a field
data.interpretation: Use thinker clusters to branch outward and explicitly represent collaborators, institutions, disagreements, and implementation communities.
data.uncertainty: A thinker can be a useful navigational node while still obscuring collective authorship, editors, translators, practitioners, and critics.

data.title: Frame Language provides neutral or final vocabulary
data.claim: Frame Language provides neutral or final vocabulary
data.interpretation: Use Frame Language as a visible analytical vocabulary open to critique, alternatives and contextual translation.
data.uncertainty: Every vocabulary reflects purposes, distinctions and exclusions and may not fit all communities or domains.

data.title: FtC residencies have supported over 80 builders
data.claim: FtC residencies have supported over 80 builders
data.interpretation: State it as an organizer-reported participation count and seek cohort, output, and follow-up records before drawing impact conclusions.
data.uncertainty: This is an organizer-reported cumulative figure without visible participant-level outcome accounting on the cited page.

data.title: Funding, reporting and analytics form a complete evidence chain
data.claim: Funding, reporting and analytics form a complete evidence chain
data.interpretation: Describe what each system records, what it cannot establish, and what additional domain evidence or affected-party review is needed.
data.uncertainty: Allocation records, grantee updates and observed metrics answer different questions and may omit real-world effects.

data.title: g0v is an organization with a single leadership or position
data.claim: g0v is an organization with a single leadership or position
data.interpretation: Describe specific projects, contributors, teams, or statements rather than attributing one position to g0v as a whole.
data.uncertainty: The community explicitly describes itself as decentralized and composed of autonomous projects without one center or representative.

data.title: GAIAI makes environmental data legible, actionable, and economically viable
data.claim: GAIAI makes environmental data legible, actionable, and economically viable
data.interpretation: GAIAI develops tools intended to improve access to and use of environmental data; practical, economic, and ecological outcomes require case-specific evidence.
data.uncertainty: This combines several distinct outcomes: data processing, user comprehension, decision utility, market design, and ecological legitimacy.

data.title: Generative and extractive systems are cleanly separable
data.claim: Generative and extractive systems are cleanly separable
data.interpretation: Treat generative/extractive as an inquiry lens and document specific value flows, harms, and benefits.
data.uncertainty: Real organizations often contain mixed incentives, value flows, labor arrangements, and ecological effects.

data.title: Global network membership proves common practice
data.claim: Global network membership proves common practice
data.interpretation: Represent network relationships separately; verify practices at regional and member level.
data.uncertainty: Membership or affiliation does not establish shared governance, quality or outcomes across diverse member organizations.

data.title: Global South and decolonial perspectives can be represented through a few pro…
data.claim: Global South and decolonial perspectives can be represented through a few prominent organizations
data.interpretation: Describe each source's scope and authority; treat regional labels as discovery groupings, not representative blocs.
data.uncertainty: The first corrective clusters remain institution-heavy and cannot stand in for territorial movements, communities, languages or political traditions.

data.title: Global South is a single coherent region or perspective
data.claim: Global South is a single coherent region or perspective
data.interpretation: Use Global South as a provisional geopolitical and power-aware grouping; preserve regional, national, local and community specificity.
data.uncertainty: The term covers highly diverse countries, peoples, political economies, languages, institutions and colonial histories.

data.title: Goat production in a semi-arid region is inherently regenerative
data.claim: Goat production in a semi-arid region is inherently regenerative
data.interpretation: Describe territorial rationale and require ecological evidence before using regenerative or agroecological labels.
data.uncertainty: Local adaptation does not establish water, forage, animal-welfare, biodiversity or emissions outcomes.

data.title: gov/acc identifies the most urgent problems in web3 governance
data.claim: gov/acc identifies the most urgent problems in web3 governance
data.interpretation: gov/acc Phase 1 surfaces governance problems reported by its participant sample; urgency scores are research signals, not ecosystem-wide consensus.
data.uncertainty: The dashboard reflects a limited set of structured interviews and a defined composite scoring method.

data.title: Gov4Git or repository governance removes the need for human institutions
data.claim: Gov4Git or repository governance removes the need for human institutions
data.interpretation: Describe technical affordances separately from governance legitimacy and real rules-in-use.
data.uncertainty: Protocols may structure proposals, ledgers and conflicts, but legitimacy, interpretation, access and accountability remain institutional and social questions.
